q: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

items.q: The student wants to introduce Mount Corva to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mount Corva is a volcano on the island of Isla Verde.
• It rises 2,940 meters above sea level.
• It last erupted in 1891.
• Scientists monitor it with seismic sensors.
c: Mount Corva, a 2,940-meter volcano on Isla Verde, last erupted in 1891.
It last erupted in 1891.
Isla Verde is an island.
Scientists monitor seismic sensors.
w: This doesn't name or describe the volcano for a new audience.
This doesn't mention the volcano.
This misstates the notes and doesn't introduce the volcano.
items.e: This choice names the volcano and gives its location, height, and last eruption.

items.q: The student wants to emphasize how the ship is used today. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Lark is a wooden sailing ship built in 1902.
• It is 34 meters long.
• It was fully restored in 2015.
• It now serves as a floating museum in Port Ellis.
c: Today, the restored Lark serves as a floating museum in Port Ellis.
The Lark was built in 1902.
The Lark is 34 meters long.
The Lark is a wooden sailing ship.
w: This gives the ship's age, not its current use.
This gives its size, not its current use.
This describes the ship, not its current use.
items.e: Only this choice states the ship's present use.

items.q: The student wants to identify the novel's setting. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mira Sol published her first novel, The Salt Road, in 2011.
• The novel won the Hale Prize for fiction.
• It is set in a desert trading town.
• It follows a family of merchants over three generations.
c: Mira Sol's novel The Salt Road is set in a desert trading town.
The Salt Road won the Hale Prize for fiction.
Mira Sol published The Salt Road in 2011.
The Salt Road follows three generations of merchants.
w: This gives an award, not the setting.
This gives a date, not the setting.
This describes the plot, not the setting.
items.e: Only this choice names the setting.

items.q: The student wants to compare how long the two cheeses are aged. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Alder cheese is made from cow's milk.
• Alder cheese is aged for three months.
• Bryn cheese is made from goat's milk.
• Bryn cheese is aged for two years.
c: Alder cheese is aged for three months, while Bryn cheese is aged for two years.
Alder cheese is made from cow's milk, and Bryn cheese from goat's milk.
Bryn cheese is aged for two years.
Both cheeses are aged.
w: This compares milk, not aging time.
This gives only one aging time.
This gives neither aging time.
items.e: Only this choice states both aging times side by side.

items.q: The student wants to explain a benefit that the dam provides to residents. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Kettle Falls Dam was completed in 1958.
• It created Lake Ardis.
• The dam supplies electricity to about 200,000 homes.
• The dam is 120 meters tall.
c: The Kettle Falls Dam supplies electricity to about 200,000 homes.
The Kettle Falls Dam was completed in 1958.
The Kettle Falls Dam is 120 meters tall.
The Kettle Falls Dam created Lake Ardis.
w: A completion date isn't a benefit.
Height isn't a benefit.
This names the lake without saying how it benefits residents.
items.e: Supplying electricity to homes is a direct benefit to residents.

items.q: The student wants to name a specific work by Matsuda and say where it can be seen. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Rui Matsuda is a painter born in 1952.
• He is known for paintings of rainy city streets.
• His painting Gray Harbor was completed in 1987.
• Gray Harbor hangs in the City Art Museum.
c: Rui Matsuda's painting Gray Harbor can be seen at the City Art Museum.
Rui Matsuda is known for paintings of rainy city streets.
Rui Matsuda was born in 1952.
Gray Harbor was completed in 1987.
w: This names no specific work or location.
This gives neither a work nor a location.
This names a work but not where it can be seen.
items.e: Only this choice names a work and its location.

items.q: The student wants to recommend a trail to a beginning hiker. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The North Trail is 4 miles long and rated easy.
• The North Trail passes a waterfall.
• The Ridge Trail is 9 miles long and rated difficult.
• The Ridge Trail offers views of the valley.
c: Beginners may prefer the North Trail, an easy 4-mile route that passes a waterfall.
The Ridge Trail offers views of the valley.
The Ridge Trail is 9 miles long and rated difficult.
The North Trail and the Ridge Trail are both in the park.
w: This promotes the harder trail without addressing beginners.
This describes the difficult trail, which doesn't suit beginners.
This isn't in the notes and makes no recommendation.
items.e: The easy, shorter trail suits a beginner, and this choice says so.

items.q: The student wants to explain what information the waggle dance conveys. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Honeybees perform a "waggle dance" after finding food.
• The angle of the dance shows the direction of the food relative to the sun.
• The length of the waggle shows the distance to the food.
• The dance was first decoded by scientist Karl von Frisch.
c: Through the angle and length of its waggle dance, a honeybee shows other bees the direction of and distance to food.
The waggle dance was first decoded by Karl von Frisch.
Honeybees perform a waggle dance after finding food.
The angle of the dance relates to the sun.
w: This is about who decoded the dance, not what it conveys.
This says when bees dance, not what the dance conveys.
This is incomplete; it omits direction to food and distance.
items.e: Only this choice explains both pieces of information the dance conveys.

items.q: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two libraries. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Eastside Library holds 40,000 books and is open six days a week.
• Westside Library holds 65,000 books and is open seven days a week.
• Both libraries offer free after-school tutoring.
c: Both the Eastside and Westside libraries offer free after-school tutoring.
Westside Library holds 25,000 more books than Eastside Library.
Eastside Library is open six days a week, and Westside is open seven.
Westside Library holds 65,000 books.
w: This emphasizes a difference.
This emphasizes a difference.
This describes only one library.
items.e: Free tutoring is the only feature the notes say both libraries share.

items.q: The student wants to present the study's findings about drivers and cyclists. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers surveyed 500 commuters about their satisfaction with their daily commute.
• Cyclists reported the highest satisfaction.
• Drivers reported the lowest satisfaction.
• Bus riders reported satisfaction between the two.
c: In a survey of 500 commuters, cyclists were the most satisfied with their commutes and drivers were the least.
Bus riders reported satisfaction between that of cyclists and drivers.
Researchers surveyed 500 commuters.
Cyclists ride bicycles to work.
w: This focuses on bus riders.
This gives no findings.
This isn't a finding from the notes.
items.e: Only this choice reports the results for both drivers and cyclists.

items.q: The student wants to present the study's main finding. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marine biologist Ada Nwosu studied coral reefs from 2019 to 2020.
• She tracked corals that had lost their color after a heat wave.
• Some corals fully recovered within a year.
• Corals in cooler, deeper water recovered fastest.
c: Nwosu found that some heat-damaged corals recovered within a year, with those in cooler, deeper water recovering fastest.
Nwosu studied coral reefs from 2019 to 2020.
Nwosu tracked corals after a heat wave.
Corals can lose their color.
w: This gives the study's dates, not its finding.
This describes the method, not the finding.
This is background, not the finding.
items.e: This choice states what Nwosu found: recovery, and where it was fastest.

items.q: The student wants to emphasize how much the town grew. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The town of Elden had a population of 4,200 in 1990.
• Its population reached 9,800 in 2020.
• Much of the growth came from new technology jobs.
• Elden is located along the Pell River.
c: Elden's population more than doubled between 1990 and 2020, rising from 4,200 to 9,800.
Elden is located along the Pell River.
Much of Elden's growth came from technology jobs.
Elden had a population of 4,200 in 1990.
w: Location says nothing about growth.
This gives the cause, not how much the town grew.
One figure can't show growth.
items.e: This choice gives both figures and stresses that the population more than doubled (9,800 is over twice 4,200).

items.q: The student wants to describe how the kalimba is played. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The kalimba is sometimes called a thumb piano.
• It has metal tines attached to a wooden board.
• Players pluck the tines with their thumbs.
• Instruments of this kind originated in Africa.
c: A kalimba is played by plucking its metal tines with the thumbs.
Instruments like the kalimba originated in Africa.
The kalimba is sometimes called a thumb piano.
A kalimba has a wooden board.
w: This gives the instrument's origin, not how it is played.
A nickname doesn't describe how it's played.
This describes construction, not playing.
items.e: Only this choice explains the playing technique.

items.q: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two novels. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Lin Hart's novel Paper Moons was published in 1999.
• Hart's novel Iron Bells was published in 2008.
• Both novels are set in small towns in Ohio.
• Iron Bells is twice as long as Paper Moons.
c: Lin Hart's novels Paper Moons and Iron Bells are both set in small towns in Ohio.
Iron Bells is twice as long as Paper Moons.
Paper Moons was published in 1999, and Iron Bells in 2008.
Paper Moons was published in 1999.
w: This emphasizes a difference.
This emphasizes a difference.
This describes one novel only.
items.e: Their shared setting is the similarity in the notes.

items.q: The student wants to present the study's results while noting where the two methods did not differ. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers compared two ways of teaching fractions for six weeks.
• Method A used visual models; Method B used memorized rules.
• Method A students scored 15 points higher on problem-solving.
• Scores on simple computation were similar for both groups.
c: Students taught with visual models outscored those who memorized rules by 15 points on problem-solving, though both groups did similarly on simple computation.
Students taught with visual models scored 15 points higher on problem-solving.
Researchers compared two methods for teaching fractions over six weeks.
Method A used visual models, while Method B used memorized rules.
w: This omits where the methods didn't differ.
This gives no results.
This describes the methods, not the results.
items.e: This choice gives both the difference and the area of no difference.

items.q: The student wants to emphasize how the bridge's use has changed over time. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Varden Bridge was built in 1889.
• At the time, it was the longest steel bridge in the region.
• It was closed to cars in 1990.
• It reopened in 2012 as a walkway for pedestrians.
c: Once used by cars, the 1889 Varden Bridge reopened in 2012 as a pedestrian walkway.
When it was built in 1889, the Varden Bridge was the region's longest steel bridge.
The Varden Bridge was closed to cars in 1990.
The Varden Bridge is made of steel.
w: This is about its size, not its changing use.
This gives only one change, without the new use.
Material isn't about use.
items.e: This choice contrasts the earlier use (cars) with the current use (pedestrians).

items.q: The student wants to explain what makes resurrection ferns unusual among ferns. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ferns reproduce using tiny spores spread by wind.
• Most fern species need moist conditions to survive and reproduce.
• Resurrection ferns can lose most of their water and appear dead.
• After rain, resurrection ferns turn green again within hours.
c: Unlike most ferns, which need moist conditions, resurrection ferns can lose most of their water and then revive after rain.
Ferns reproduce using spores spread by wind.
Resurrection ferns turn green after rain.
Most fern species need moist conditions.
w: This applies to ferns in general.
This omits the contrast with other ferns.
This describes typical ferns, not the unusual ones.
items.e: Being unusual requires a contrast with typical ferns, and only this choice makes it.

items.q: The student wants to contrast the overall rate of daily print reading with the rate among older adults. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A survey asked 1,000 adults about their news habits.
• 62% read news online daily.
• 18% read a print newspaper daily.
• Among adults over 65, 41% read a print newspaper daily.
c: While only 18% of all surveyed adults read a print newspaper daily, 41% of those over 65 did.
62% of surveyed adults read news online daily.
41% of adults over 65 read a print newspaper daily.
A survey asked 1,000 adults about their news habits.
w: This is about online reading.
This gives only the older group's rate.
This gives no rates.
items.e: The goal requires both rates, set against each other.
